assumption_register.statement: Ideal dimension set is finite and every dimension is equally important

conceptual.anchor: Level 1 - Difference: Delta(K,I) 'What is different?' Level 2 - Deficit/severity: S(Delta,P) 'How important is this difference for purpose P?' Level 3 - Distance, if mathematically justified: d(K,I) 'How far apart are these states under a formally defined metric?'

formal.anchor: Distance \neq Single Number ... Distance = A Multidimensional Measurement ... d(K_t,I_t) = (d_Dim, d_Value, d_Epistemic, d_Relationship, d_Coherence, d_State, d_Constraint, d_Performance)

governance.anchor: the next mathematical question should actually be: What is the mathematical structure of an epistemic difference? That question comes before what is its numerical distance? and will determine whether KnowledgeOS needs metrics, partial orders, lattices, graph differences, or a combination.

rationale_evidence.anchor: D_E(K_t,I^K_t) \rightarrow 0 \not\Rightarrow Journey Complete ... I^K_2 \neq I^K_0 ... Knowledge acquisition can move the Ideal State. KnowledgeOS is not solving a static optimization problem. It is solving a dynamic epistemic navigation problem.
rationale_evidence.statement: Shows via the Arjuna example that measured distance reaching zero (D_E(K_2,I^K_0)=0) does not mean the epistemic journey is complete, because the Ideal State itself evolved in step (I^K_2 != I^K_0); reframes KnowledgeOS's problem as dynamic epistemic navigation rather than static optimization against a fixed target.

rationale_evidence.anchor: MissingKnowledge -> EpistemicDeficiency -> UnderstandingGap ... We did not simply move from distance 7 to distance 4. We transformed the problem. This is precisely why a scalar is inadequate as the fundamental representation.
rationale_evidence.statement: Uses the Arjuna case to show the discrepancy's TYPE, not just its magnitude, changes as investigation proceeds (a missing-dimension gap becomes an epistemic-support deficiency once the relationship is observed, then an understanding gap once the normative implication is recognized) -- direct evidence that a scalar distance would hide the qualitative nature of what actually changed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Discrepancy(K,I) != Discrepancy(I,K) because the Ideal State is normative and the Knowledge State is descriptive. Therefore the relationship is fundamentally directional: K -> I, not symmetric.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues discrepancy comparison is fundamentally directional/asymmetric (comparing current-to-ideal is not the same operation as ideal-to-current, since one side is normative and the other descriptive), reinforcing that discrepancy cannot be assumed a symmetric metric and must instead be treated as a structured comparison relation with numerical distance only an optional derived, non-fundamental measure.

## Rationale
Shows via the Arjuna example that measured distance reaching zero (D_E(K_2,I^K_0)=0) does not mean the epistemic journey is complete, because the Ideal State itself evolved in step (I^K_2 != I^K_0); reframes KnowledgeOS's problem as dynamic epistemic navigation rather than static optimization against a fixed target. [S0791] Uses the Arjuna case to show the discrepancy's TYPE, not just its magnitude, changes as investigation proceeds (a missing-dimension gap becomes an epistemic-support deficiency once the relationship is observed, then an understanding gap once the normative implication is recognized) -- direct evidence that a scalar distance would hide the qualitative nature of what actually changed. [S0799] Argues discrepancy comparison is fundamentally directional/asymmetric (comparing current-to-ideal is not the same operation as ideal-to-current, since one side is normative and the other descriptive), reinforcing that discrepancy cannot be assumed a symmetric metric and must instead be treated as a structured comparison relation with numerical distance only an optional derived, non-fundamental measure. [S0802]

- [S0792] types=[DEFINITION, RESTATEMENT] scope=OBJECT — "Formalizes the Difference-vs-Distance split as the working model: Compare produces a structured Delta (per-component difference sets/structures for dimension, value, epistemic, relationship and coherence), and a separate Measure function produces a scalar D; Zero's canonical role is Compare (difference detection), not Measure (quantification)."
